Production and consumption of natural gas increased relative to the preceding year, growing by 3.2
percent and 3.6 percent to 63,440.5 million Standard Cubic Feet (MMSCF) and 61,956.7 MMSCF,
respectively (Table 3.13 and Chart 3.2). This outturn was largely driven by rising gas demand from
industries, coupled with continued growth in the number of vehicles using Compressed Natural Gas
(CNG) to 16,354 in 2025/26 from 7,000 in 2024/25. Likewise, the CNG filling stations increased to
19 from 9 stations4. Power-generating plants accounted for the largest share of consumption at 70.1
percent, followed by industries at 27.6 percent.
4
The CNG filling stations are located in Dar es Salaam (16), Mtwara (1), Pwani (1) and Ruvuma (1)

4.0 GOVERNMENT REVENUE PERFORMANCE
4.1 Tax Revenue Collections
Tax revenue collection demonstrated robust performance in 2025/26, reaching TZS 36,250.4 billion,
exceeding the annual target by 7.1 percent (Table 4.1). This performance was largely supported
by expansion of economic activities, and improved tax compliance following enhanced taxpayers’
education and sustained government efforts in improving tax administration, including the use of
Integrated Domestic Revenue Administration System. Taxes on local goods and services accounted
